title: Inhibitory circuits control leg movements during Drosophila grooming (Syed, Ravbar, Simpson; preprint 10.1101/2024.06.05.597468)
why: Cites Harris 2015 and Soffers 2025. Its own CsChrimson activation of 13A and 13B neurons (R35G04-GAL4-DBD, GAD-GAL4-AD and other split lines) in intact, dusted and headless adults. Reported: reduced grooming, front-leg extension, poor leg coordination; pulsed activation of six 13A neurons induces grooming and walking. The paper calls these 13A/13B 'subsets', so likely partial_or_mixed. CAUTION: the paper contains a computational model; read only the experimental sections and figure legends.

title: Central processing of leg proprioception in Drosophila (Agrawal et al.)
why: Cites Harris 2015. Its own CsChrimson activation of split-GAL4 lines for 13Bα, 9Aα and 10Bα neurons, in headless flies (leg joint movements; Fig 3 and Fig 6) and walking flies (slowing or stopping with 10Bα; Fig 8). These are cell-type subsets named within hemilineages; 9Aα lines may also label 9Aα2 cells.

title: Selective presynaptic inhibition of leg proprioception in behaving Drosophila (Dallmann et al.; preprint 10.1101/2023.10.20.563322)
why: Cites Harris 2015. Its own leg-specific optogenetic silencing AND activation of GABAergic 9A neurons in tethered walking flies (an Extended Data figure shows activation examples). The 9A line targets about 10 neurons per front-leg neuromere, so it is a subset of 9A. The activation outcome was not confirmed in the text I read. CAUTION: the paper has a modelling section (descending-neuron stimulation recruiting 9A); avoid it.

title: Extensive and diverse patterns of cell death sculpt neural networks in insects (Pop et al.)
why: Cites Harris 2015. TrpA1 activation of MARCM clones of 'undead' hemilineage 0B neurons (cell death blocked) in decapitated adult males: walking in 9/17 (Fig 4). The positive control is TDC2-GAL4 (octopaminergic neurons, not a hemilineage). This is clonal activation of undead cells, not the normal hemilineage.

title: A central somatotopic map of the fly leg supports spatially targeted grooming (Elabbady et al.; preprint 10.64898/2026.02.27.708590)
why: Cites Harris 2015. Search snippets report its own optogenetic activation of hemilineage 23B interneuron subsets (distal-sensing vs proximal-sensing 23B) eliciting targeted grooming (e.g. 96% front leg vs 68% front/32% middle leg). Subsets, not whole 23B. Full text not opened (the paper relies on connectome analysis); the coder should check its experimental sections only.

title: Unc-4 acts to promote neuronal identity and development of the take-off circuit in the Drosophila CNS (Lacin et al.)
why: REJECTED: only loss of function (unc-4 removal in 7B, ablation) and take-off assays. Activation of 7B/2A is cited from Harris 2015, not performed here (checked full-text XML, first 100k characters).

title: Single-cell type analysis of wing premotor circuits in the ventral nerve cord of Drosophila melanogaster (Ehrhardt et al.)
why: REJECTED: CsChrimson activation is only of sparse wing motoneuron lines in tethered flight. Interneuron/hemilineage lines are anatomy only; hemilineage activation is cited from earlier work.

title: Doublesex regulates the connectivity of a neural circuit controlling Drosophila male courtship song (Shirangi et al.)
why: REJECTED (likely): manipulates the single dsx+ cell type TN1A, not a named hemilineage. Abstract only; whether it does adult activation is unconfirmed.
hemilineages_as_named: TN1A (12A-derived per other sources; not named in abstract)
